$comment: Capability declarations for repository tooling that a user is expected to execute directly. Skills carry their own declaration inside attestation.json so they stay auditable after being copied out of this repository; these files are not skills, so they declare here. scripts/audit_skill_safety.py checks each declaration against what the code can actually do.

components.rationale: Reads SKILL.md, attestation.json and evals/test-cases.json and prints a report. Writes nothing.
Parses skill sources with ast and scans Markdown with re. Writes nothing, fetches nothing, and executes nothing it reads -- an auditor that ran the code it audits would be pointless.

Declared 'unrestricted' deliberately: this is the only tool here that writes OUTSIDE the repository, into agent skill directories under the user's home (~/.claude/skills, ~/.gemini/config/skills). It replaces a destination directory when a skill of the same name already exists. Run it with --dry-run first; it refuses to install any skill that fails the safety audit.

Copies skills/<skill>/ into .agents/skills/<skill>/ and removes mirror directories with no canonical source. Writes and deletes only inside the repository's .agents/skills/. Dry run by default; --write applies.

Makes read-only HTTPS GETs to pypi.org, api.github.com and registry.npmjs.org to find the latest version of each pin. With --write it rewrites version strings in requirements-dev.txt and .github/workflows/*.yml, and nothing else. Every fetched value must fully match a strict version or SHA pattern before it is compared or written, because these files are executed by CI. Dry run by default.
